{{Short description|Proposal in harmonic analysis}}
In [[harmonic analysis]], a branch of [[mathematics]], the '''Mizohata–Takeuchi conjecture''' proposed a weighted [[L^2 space|<math>L^2</math>]] inequality for the [[Fourier extension operator]] associated with a [[hypersurface#Smooth hypersurface|smooth hypersurface]] in Euclidean space. It asserted that the <math>L^2</math> norm of the extension of a function <math>f</math> from the hypersurface to <math>\mathbb{R}^n</math> could be bounded, for any nonnegative [[weight function]], by a constant multiple of the <math>L^2</math> norm of <math>f</math>, with the constant depending only on the supremum of the weight over certain tube-shaped regions.{{efn|Here a “tube” means a long, thin cylindrical region in <math>\mathbb R^n</math>, typically of fixed radius and arbitrary length, as in the [[Kakeya set|Kakeya problem]].}}{{Citation needed|date=August 2025}} The conjecture was disproved in 2025 by [[Hannah Cairo]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hartnett |first=Kevin |date=2025-08-01 |title=At 17, Hannah Cairo Solved a Major Math Mystery |url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/at-17-hannah-cairo-solved-a-major-math-mystery-20250801/ |access-date=2025-08-08 |website=Quanta Magazine |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite arXiv | last1=Cairo | first1=Hannah |author-link1=Hannah Cairo | title=A Counterexample to the Mizohata-Takeuchi Conjecture | date=2025 | class=math.CA | eprint=2502.06137 }}</ref>

The [[conjecture]]<ref>{{cite arXiv | last1=Barceló | first1=Juan Antonio | last2=Ruiz | first2=Alberto | last3=Vilela | first3=Mari Cruz | last4=Wright | first4=Jim | title=A priori estimates of Mizohata-Takeuchi type for the Navier-Lamé operator | date=2025-01-17 | class=math.AP | eprint=2501.10133 }}</ref> originally arose in the study of well-posedness for dispersive [[partial differential equations]]. In the 1970s and 1980s Jiro Takeuchi was studying the initial value problem associated with a perturbed version of the linear [[Schrödinger equation]]. He at one point claimed<ref name="Takeuchi Mizohata">{{cite journal | last=Takeuchi | first=Jiro | title=Some remarks on my paper "On the Cauchy problem for some non-kowalewskian equations with distinct characteristic roots", (Schrödinger equations and generalizations, I) | journal=Kyoto Journal of Mathematics | volume=24 | issue=4 | date=1984-01-01 | issn=2156-2261 | doi=10.1215/kjm/1250521231 | doi-access=free | url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/journal-of-mathematics-of-kyoto-university/volume-24/issue-4/Some-remarks-on-my-paper-On-the-Cauchy-problem-for/10.1215/kjm/1250521231.pdf | access-date=2025-08-16 | pages=741–754}}</ref> a well-posed condition in <math>L^2(\mathbb{R}^n)</math> that was both necessary and sufficient for the associated [[Cauchy problem]]. [[Sigeru Mizohata]] noticed<ref name="Mizohata">{{cite book | last=Mizohata | first=Sigeru | title=On the Cauchy Problem | publisher=Academic Press | publication-place=Orlando | date=1985 | isbn=978-0-12-501660-5}}</ref> that Takeuchi’s argument was not compelling and showed that Takeuchi’s condition is necessary, but whether it is also sufficient remained open.
